shared_elements: low-relief carving on a flat stone surface
repeated row of similar motifs along the upper edge
animals or creatures with heads in profile (B)
raised arms/hands (A human hands; B animal forelimbs)
justification: Both surfaces are low-relief carvings organised with figures in profile and a horizontal banded division, and both use a row of repeated motifs along an upper edge, but these are generic compositional habits rather than shared iconography. A depicts bearded human figures with elaborate headgear, curled hair and hands raised toward one another, whereas B depicts schematic quadrupeds, a bird-like creature and abstract signs with no human presence, and the rendering conventions (dense naturalistic detailing versus flat outlined silhouettes) are quite different.
